# Explore freely; distinguish exploration from confirmation {#sec-session-06}

**Meeting 6 | Tuesday, October 13, 2026 | 1:00-2:00 PM Pacific**

## Central question

How can we learn from looking at data without misrepresenting a pattern found after inspection as a prediction made beforehand?

## The paper pair

Every citation on this page links to its full record on the [bibliography](../references.qmd) page, which is generated from `references.bib`; the [reading library](../reading-library.qmd) adds access notes and the optional extensions by meeting.

**Pairing type:** Exploratory analysis / evidential discipline.

### Paper A: The Future of Data Analysis

@tukey1962. **The Annals of Mathematical Statistics (1962).** [Paper / publisher record](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoms/1177704711)

Read the opening discussion of data analysis as an empirical activity and selected examples in Tukey; the full 67 pages are optional.

*Access: Publisher/DOI page; full text may require institutional access.*

### Paper B: The preregistration revolution

@nosek2018. **Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2018).** [Paper / publisher record](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5856500/) | [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1708274114)

Read Nosek and colleagues in full, concentrating on prediction, postdiction, and transparent separation of analyses.

*Access: Free full text in PubMed Central.*

### Why these papers belong together

Tukey makes room for data-driven inquiry. Nosek and colleagues argue for clearer evidential status through preregistration. This is a complementary pairing, not exploration versus legitimate science. [@tukey1962; @nosek2018]

### Discussant-led paper

One rotating discussant takes the following in depth and brings its argument into the discussion; everyone else reads the abstract.


## Prepare before the meeting

Bring an exploratory figure and list every major choice made after seeing the data. Do not include confidential data in public course materials.

## Discussion questions

1. When is a discovered pattern a useful question rather than a confirmed finding?
2. How do we document previous access to an existing dataset?
3. What independent evidence is available when laboratory replication is impossible?

## One-hour meeting

| Time | Activity |
|:--|:--|
| 0-10 min | Independent first judgments; surface disagreements. |
| 10-25 min | Compare the papers: claim, evidence, assumptions, and limits. The discussant presents the discussant-led paper in this block. |
| 25-45 min | Work through the case exercise below. |
| 45-55 min | Translate the discussion into agent requirements and tests. |
| 55-60 min | Record an output and one unresolved disagreement. |

### Case exercise

Run a paper exercise on the same messy Earth-science dataset: propose plots and candidate questions, then freeze a claim and its test before revealing a reserved period or region. Discuss why spatially or temporally dependent records may make a random row split misleading.

## Agent-design or evaluation output

Discovery Agent v0 rubric plus an exploration-to-confirmation handoff: log the exploratory search, freeze the new claim, specify independent evidence, and retain negative outcomes.

## Optional extensions

- @ioannidis2005: [Why Most Published Research Findings Are False](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0020124). PLoS Medicine (2005). The statistical argument that flexible, exploratory analysis with low prior odds produces mostly false positives. The strongest published case for a hypothesis gate; the seminar owes it a hearing.
- @schorlemmer2018: [The Collaboratory for the Study of Earthquake Predictability: Achievements and Priorities](https://doi.org/10.1785/0220180053). Seismological Research Letters (2018). Preregistration in this group's own field: forecasting models are submitted in advance and scored against earthquakes that have not yet happened. What a gate looks like when it is built as infrastructure.
- @rzhetsky2015: [Choosing experiments to accelerate collective discovery](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1509757112). Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (2015). Models how biochemists choose what to study next and shows that the community's actual strategy is far from the most efficient one for mapping a network. An exploration policy tested against the record, and directly usable for the agent design.
- @leonelli2014: [What difference does quantity make? On the epistemology of Big Data in biology](https://doi.org/10.1177/2053951714534395). Big Data & Society (2014). Data-intensive research does not remove theory; it moves theory into curation and classification. Relevant to what an agent inherits when it inherits a dataset.
- @bergen2019: [Machine learning for data-driven discovery in solid Earth geoscience](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aau0323). Science (2019). The field's own review of machine learning as an exploratory instrument, including where it found signals nobody predicted and where it fit noise.

## Record after the meeting

Record the evidence for your main claim, what changed your mind, what remains unresolved, and one change to the agent or its evaluation. Add the episode’s row to the [inquiry-mode ledger](../notes.qmd#inquiry-mode-ledger). Keep confidential examples in private group notes rather than committing them to this public book.
